This changes presentation only. Nivara stays installed under the same package name, so Android\'s settings, the package manager and any device or work-profile management tool still list it, and it is not a way to hide Nivara or any other application from someone who looks. It is not a security boundary and not a secret: your credential, biometric unlock, App Lock and the session timeout are what protect you, and none of them changes.

However Nivara is named right now, it can always be opened: from its launcher entry, or from Android\'s application list, where it is still Nivara. It opens on Nivara\'s home screen, and this screen is one card down from there. If you forget which name you chose, Android\'s settings still say Nivara. Nothing about reaching Nivara is hidden, and no code or gesture is needed to find it.
Unlock Nivara to change its identity. You can look at this screen without unlocking.

Choose the folder Nivara keeps its encrypted vault in. Nivara only touches the folder you pick.
Nivara does not have a vault yet, and does not create one on its own. Choose the folder that should hold it, then create the vault there.

Nivara\'s record of which folder holds the vault cannot be read, so it cannot say where the vault is. Nothing has been deleted, and no other folder has been used. Choose the folder again to reconnect to it.
This folder does not hold a Nivara vault yet. You can create one here; nothing else in the folder is touched.
The vault in this folder is intact and can be opened. Its contents are encrypted with a key that never leaves the device, and nothing else is stored here.

There is a Nivara vault in this folder, and its metadata cannot be read: the record may be damaged, or the device key that protects it may no longer be the one it was written with. Nothing has been changed, deleted or replaced, and the vault has not been treated as empty.

Nivara\'s structure is in this folder without a complete vault record, which usually means an earlier setup did not finish. Nothing has been deleted. If you expected an existing vault here, stop and check the folder before creating one.
The vault in this folder is intact, and the device key that protects its key material is no longer available — this happens when the screen lock is removed. Nothing has been changed or deleted.
This folder holds a vault written by a newer version of Nivara. This build refuses to touch it rather than risk your data. Update Nivara to open it.
The folder that holds the vault cannot be reached right now — the storage may be removed, or the folder may no longer exist. Nothing has been changed or deleted.
Nivara no longer has permission to use this folder. Choose it again to grant access; nothing has been changed or deleted.
This deletes the unreadable records in this folder and starts a new vault. Anything the old vault held cannot be recovered.

The vault is one folder on storage you choose, and Nivara only ever touches that folder. Inside it, Nivara keeps an authenticated record of the vault and an encrypted content area; nothing is written anywhere else and nothing is uploaded. The folder can be on a memory card or in a synced location, which is also how it moves between devices — and why the storage is not a secret: what protects it is the encryption, not where it sits.
